entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Quintus Tineius Clemens, a distinguished Roman senator, held the prestigious office of Consul Ordinarius in AD 195, serving alongside Publius Julius Scapula Tertullus Priscus. His career unfolded during the tumultuous yet consolidating years of the Severan Dynasty, a period marked by civil conflict and the subsequent re-establishment of imperial authority under Septimius Severus. As a member of the senatorial aristocracy, Clemens represented the enduring administrative and political class that underpinned the vast Roman Empire, providing continuity and expertise amidst shifts in imperial power.

Clemens's consulship in AD 195 placed him at the heart of Roman governance during a pivotal moment. This year saw Septimius Severus consolidating his power after defeating rivals Pescennius Niger and preparing for the final confrontation with Clodius Albinus. While specific details of Clemens's actions during his consulship are sparse, his holding of the highest annual magistracy signifies his loyalty and standing within the new Severan order. He likely participated in the routine legislative and judicial functions of the Senate, contributing to the administrative stability that allowed Severus to focus on military campaigns and securing the empire's frontiers. Scholars also speculate that he may have later served as a proconsul, potentially governing provinces like Asia or Bithynia et Pontus, further illustrating his role in the broader imperial administration.
